title: Audit and persist external provider sign-in outcomes consistently
description:
Problem: local password sign-in records both login-history rows and audit-log entries, but the current external OAuth callback path is not held to the same contract. In `MemorySmith.App/Program.cs`, the GitHub `OnCreatingTicket` handler writes a successful `LoginHistoryEntry` with hashed IP/user-agent metadata and `RequestId`, but does not emit a corresponding audit event. The `OnRemoteFailure` handler redirects to `/login` or `/profile` without recording either an audit-log entry or a failed login-history row. This leaves admin audit/history surfaces incomplete for external-provider authentication activity and makes provider sign-in failures harder to investigate than local-auth failures.

Evidence from 2026-05-26 audit:
- `SecurityServices.SignInAsync()` records `auth.login.failed` and `auth.login.succeeded` through `AuditLogService` and also appends login history.
- `Program.cs` GitHub `OnCreatingTicket` appends a successful `LoginHistoryEntry`, but there is no `AuditLogService` call in that callback.
- `Program.cs` `OnRemoteFailure` handles the response by redirecting, but does not persist an audit or login-history failure record.
- No focused task or test coverage was found for external-provider sign-in audit parity.

Desired outcome: successful and failed external-provider sign-in attempts should be durably visible to operators with the same privacy posture as local sign-ins.

Scope:
- In scope: GitHub OAuth callback success/failure auditing, login-history parity for external-provider failures where enough context exists, provider/link-conflict and disabled-user failure cases, and request-metadata propagation through the external-auth path.
- In scope: reuse the existing privacy-reviewed request metadata pattern; do not store raw OAuth access tokens, raw IP addresses, or raw user-agent strings.
- Out of scope: changing provider credential storage, OAuth scopes, or broad auth UX beyond operator-visible audit/history completeness.

Acceptance criteria:
- Successful external-provider sign-ins record an audit event with provider context and the same persisted request-metadata contract used elsewhere.
- External-provider failures that currently short-circuit with redirects or `ctx.Fail(...)` produce durable, operator-visible audit evidence and a failure login-history row when a provider/subject outcome can be identified safely.
- Persisted details remain privacy-conscious and do not include raw tokens or third-party profile payloads beyond the minimum identifiers already in use.
- Focused tests cover at least one successful external-provider sign-in path and one failure path.

Validation:
- Add focused auth/storage tests for external-provider success and failure persistence.
- Run the affected auth/admin/storage test slice.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task creation/update.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during 2026-05-26 audit after comparing local-password auth auditing with the GitHub OAuth callback path in startup and finding missing external-provider audit/failure persistence.
